Q: How to use images when it comes to SQL databases? A:

Question #1: How to store image in a MySQL table

MySQL supports blob data types, allowing you to store images or any other kind of binary data. There are 4 such types which only vary in sizes:

  • TINYBLOB : up to 255 bytes, best for keeping very tiny icons or flags
  • BLOB : up 64 KB, for things like small GIF/JPEG images, normal size documents
  • MEDIUMBLOB : up to 16 MB, enough to keep most PDF files and photo images or music MP3s
  • LONGBLOB : up to 4 GB, should be enough to hold videos

So far there's no larger blob type available in MySQL yet.

See also:

  • https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/8.4/en/blob.html
  • https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/8.4/en/storage-requirements.html

Store image to blob column

To create a table with a blob column enough to keep a normal size image:

CREATE TABLE data_table (
  id   INT AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY,
  name VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL, -- eg. 'family-gathering.jpg'
  mime VARCHAR(80) NOT NULL,  -- eg. 'image/jpeg'
  data MEDIUMBLOB NOT NULL
);

If your image is already stored in a location where DB server can directly access to, this is the statement to store the image data into DB:

INSERT INTO data_table(name, mime, data)
VALUES('family-gathering.jpg', 'image/jpg', LOAD_FILE('/path-to-the-file/family-gathering.jpg'));

But oftentimes that is not the case and the data is actually only available on the application server, not DB server. You can pass the data just like ordinary column data in your SQL query. The following is a possible example code written in C#:

using System.IO;
using MySql.Data.MySqlClient;

// prepare variables host, db, account, db, dirPath, fileName...

byte[] data = File.ReadAllBytes($"{dirPath}/{fileName}");
using (var conn = new MySqlConnection($"Server={host};Database={db};User ID={account};Password={pw};"))
{
    conn.Open();
    string sql = """
                 INSERT INTO data_table(name, mime, data)
                 VALUES (@name, @mime, @data)
                 """;
    using var cmd = new MySqlCommand(sql, conn);
    cmd.Parameters.AddWithValue("@name", fileName);
    cmd.Parameters.AddWithValue("@mime", "image/jpg");
    cmd.Parameters.Add("@data", MySqlDbType.MediumBlob).Value = data;
    cmd.ExecuteNonQuery();
}

Retrieve image from blob column

Just like any other types of data, like so:

SELECT name, mime, data
FROM data_table
WHERE id = 1234;

Or if you want to store it on certain location in DB server:

SELECT data
INTO DUMPFILE '/path-to-the-output-file/saved-family-gathering.jpg'
FROM data_table
WHERE id = 1234;

As explained in:

  • https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/8.0/en/select-into.html

But generally this is not the preferred solution, not only it saves the data on DB server, it's also saved with a fixed name in certain directory path. And currently due to MySQL's limitation we cannot use a variable in the INTO DUMPFILE clause. That means in a multi-user DB server it is highly likely to have a collision problem.

The preferred way is to use the ordinary SELECT without INTO DUMPFILE and the application code should receive the blob data and store it on application side.

Question #2: Store image on an external storage

It is quite common practice to store large data files, such as images, outside of a database server. DB servers are not the most efficient storage solution for such task. Instead, you can use a service specifically designed for the purpose and AWS S3 is one such option. However, be prepared that cloud storage services would charge for storage fees one way or another.

If you decide to go this route, you need to design the table columns to store the image's identity info such as the resource path on the storage service and the resource ID. Also the storage service typically would require an authentication key or token so your application can access the data. It is strongly recommended not to keep this authentication info in DB to avoid potential security risks. Instead, your program should be designed so that the authentication credentials are retrieved from a secure source or obtained dynamically from the storage service as a one‑time access key or token.

Q: Wooslider/Flexslider Respnsive Image not working A:

It appears from reading around trying to resolve this issue that at some point flexslider added a style attribute to images containing the height and width of the image, resulting in any CSS aimed at altering the size rendered useless.

I simply added this after the call to initialise flexslider:

$(this).find('li img').removeAttr('style');

This removes any style attributes from the images, and then the width can be controlled by CSS.
